title: PR sculpting journal — lightweight review heuristics
content:
Purpose: quick personal notebook for small PRs I review or open. Not a formal playbook — capture what actually helps me move things fast and safe.

Top-level heuristics (mental checklist, do these first):
- safety: any data leakage / logging change? (if yes, stop and escalate)
- tests: does CI exercise the critical path (happy path + one error case)?
- surface area: can this be split smaller? aim for < 300 LOC change whenever practical
- docs: smoke update to README or migration note if behaviour changes
- perf: obvious O(n^2) / expensive loops flagged with comment + TODO for benchmarks

Quick review template (copy-paste into PR comment):
1) Summary: what I think this does in one sentence
2) Risk: buyer-caveats / blast radius
3) Tests: are there unit/integration tests that cover the change? if not, add a short list of minimal tests
4) Suggestion: a single, concrete code suggestion or smaller PR split

Common refactor ideas I keep coming back to (sketches):
- extract a thin adapter for model config parsing (ServConfig) — isolates parsing + validation so callers can assume canonical model config objects
- replace ad-hoc backoff in retry logic with a BackoffPolicy class (makes metrics + testing simpler)
- move queue-length metrics upstream from worker to router so we can make routing decisions without peeking into worker internals

Small experimental notes (notes-to-self while prototyping):
- tried caching parsed-config objects in request context: reduced allocations but increased GC churn on high QPS. next: benchmark object pooling vs ephemeral objects.
- quick micro-benchmark: 1k concurrent requests to local runtime, swapping string concatenation to StringBuilder equiv gave ~6% CPU reduction. worth upstreaming? maybe for hot path only.

Follow-ups / TODOs (prioritized):
- [ ] Create INF ticket to centralize model config parsing (INF-1029 reference) — owner: Matteo — due: 2026-03-14
- [ ] Add a lightweight integration test for retry policy (target: cover exponential backoff boundary) — owner: Noelle
- [ ] Draft a short note for Console team about exposing queue-length metric (ping @Aisha for ops POV)

Edge cases & open questions (brain-dump):
- Are we okay with mild semantic drift when canonicalizing configs? need a migration note.
- Can a BackoffPolicy be expressed as config (json) or is code required for fine-grained hooks? my leaning: config for simple, code for custom hooks.
- How to handle partial failures during rollout (canary)? current fallback policy is coarse; maybe add per-route severity mapping.

Practical review micro-hacks (shortcuts I use during triage):
- skim changelog and commit messages first (fast signal)
- search for TODOs and FIXME in the diff (often reveal work-in-progress)
- large generated files? request they be in a separate commit or excluded from review (add .gitattributes / build artifacts)

Sample quick PR comment (boilerplate):
"Thanks! Overall looks straightforward. I think we should split the large config parsing change into two PRs: (1) parse+validate only + tests, (2) integration + migration. Reason: smaller rollback surface and faster review. Also please add a one-liner to RELEASE_NOTES.md describing the user-visible change."

Notes about tone and cadence: keep comments prescriptive and single-action ("please split X into Y") rather than laundry lists. If a PR needs > 3 substantive changes, ask author to break it up and propose an owner for follow-up.

Historic crumbs (keep for context):
- earlier attempt to centralize parsing landed in https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1920 but rolled back due to migration gaps
- Slack thread with ops around queue metrics: see linked_artifacts above

End-of-day quick checklist before merging a small PR:
- [ ] CI green across all supported runners
- [ ] Smoke run locally with minimal script (./scripts/smoke-local.sh)
- [ ] Short changelog entry + test added or ticket opened

Random TODOs to move to tickets later:
- rework retry tests so they don't depend on real time (use fake clock)
- add lint rule to flag utility functions > 200 LOC

If I revisit this in one month: measure whether the per-PR split guidance reduced average review size (target: -25% LOC per PR) and whether the number of post-merge fixes decreased.
